title: PRD Addendum v3 — Watchlist Redesign: Standalone Shell, Two-View Watchlist, Bond Field Upgrade, Drawer, Alerts Panel, Settings (D33-D34)

sections.heading: Change Record
sections.body: markdown: addendum v3.0 extends addendum v2 (which extends addendum v1, which extends PRD_DK_Bond_Tracker_v2) after owner decisions D33 (standalone watchlist redesign) and D34 (Settings screen) of 2026-10-30; adds FR-38..FR-49; no legacy FR altered — FR-01..FR-24 remain owned by PRD_DK_Bond_Tracker_v2, FR-25/FR-26 remain owned by addendum v1, and FR-27..FR-37 remain owned by addendum v2. Wave-3 scope covers: a standalone desktop-style app shell (D33), a two-view watchlist with Move-to-Holdings (D33), the bond master field set upgrade stored per position (D33), watchlist table filters/search/sort/density (D33), the per-position detail drawer (D33), the watchlist alerts panel fed by the credit-day engine (D33), the Settings screen — Email Alerts, Alert Preferences, General, Data, About (D34), and shell integration of counts, email status and privacy masking (D33+D34).

sections.heading: Design Source
sections.body: The watchlist redesign UI truth is the confirmed mockup v1 (.IDE_Plans/design_drafts/watchlist_standalone_mockup_v1.html): standalone shell chrome, segmented My Holdings / Watching tabs, summary strip, filter chips, dense table with status left-borders and right-aligned Indian-format money, detail drawer, alerts rail, Watching cards with Move to Holdings, sidebar privacy toggle and bottom status bar. The Settings screen lands as mockup v2 in parallel; the Settings requirements and detail sections in THIS document are based on decision D34 text (SMTP + alert preferences + general + data + about; credentials local-only, masked).

sections.heading: Standalone App Shell (D33)
sections.body: The watchlist redesign ships as a standalone desktop-style app, not a website: fake-native window chrome (titlebar with menu strip and window buttons), a left sidebar navigation (Dashboard, Month Grid, Watchlist, Financial Goals, Alerts, Reports/Print, Settings — Settings is a real destination), and a bottom status bar. The connection chip reads 'Offline — local database' to keep the offline honesty visible at all times.

sections.heading: Two-View Watchlist (D33)
sections.body: The Watchlist page carries two views behind a segmented pill switcher: 'My Holdings' (owned positions, with row count) and 'Watching' (candidates being evaluated — not owned, research only, with its own count). Each Watching card shows name, ISIN, rating badge with agency, coupon, yield, payout cycle and a 'Move to Holdings' action; moving an item converts it into a held position that then appears in the monthly grid and dashboard and updates both tab counts. The drawer's 'Mark as Watching ⇄' action provides the reverse move.

sections.heading: Bond Master Field Set Upgrade (D33)
sections.body: The bond master gains a research-grade field set stored PER POSITION: credit rating plus rating agency (badge pair, e.g. AA- CRISIL), coupon %, expected yield % (manual offline entry, labeled as such in the UI), payout cycle (Monthly/Quarterly/Annual), issuer type (Corporate Bond / NCD / SDI / Govt), secured flag, and face value. These fields power the table columns, the filter chips, the Watching cards and the detail drawer.

sections.heading: Watchlist Table — Filters, Search, Sort, Density (D33)
sections.body: The holdings table offers filter chips for Rating (AA-family), Payout cycle, Issuer type and Status (Danger / On-going / Completed / Watching), a text search by company name or ISIN (e.g. Alpha Securities Ltd, INE9000A01001), column sorting (rating, maturity, etc.), active-filter chips with remove, and a Compact/Comfortable density switch. Monetary columns are right-aligned in Indian numbering format (₹1,50,000.00); each status is indicated by a colored left border on the row (Danger red, selected accent) so status is readable at a glance; the footer shows visible-row counts and the active density.

sections.heading: Position Detail Drawer (D33)
sections.body: Clicking a table row selects it and opens the right-rail detail drawer for that position: facts grid (ISIN, face value, secured, issuer type, credit rating + agency, start date, end date, credit day with payout cycle), a payment schedule (received / overdue / upcoming rows with amounts), a yield/investment summary (invested, returned, coupon, expected yield), and three actions — Edit Position, Record Payment (primary), Mark as Watching ⇄. The drawer carries the offline honesty note: ratings/prices are entered manually, no live feed.

sections.heading: Watchlist Alerts Panel (D33)
sections.body: The right rail below the drawer hosts the watchlist alerts panel, fed by the day-wise credit-day engine (D22/FR-33) and the in-app notification history (FR-34): red cards for payout overdue, amber cards for payout due-soon, and accent cards for maturity-soon, each dismissible. Dismissing removes the card from the panel only — the notification history row with its timestamp is retained for audit. Affected table rows carry a red alert dot.

sections.heading: Settings — Email Alerts (D34)
sections.body: Settings > Email Alerts is the SMTP configuration screen: SMTP host (default smtp.gmail.com), port select with security mode (465 SSL / 587 STARTTLS), username, App Password (masked on entry, never displayed back — 'stored locally, never shown again'), recipient alert address, and from-name; a Test Email button and a Save button; a status badge showing 'Not configured' (red dot) or 'Configured' (green). Credentials stay on this machine in the local database (alert_prefs); environment variables SMTP_USER / SMTP_APP_PASSWORD still override stored values. No cloud, no accounts.

sections.heading: Settings — Alert Preferences (D34)
sections.body: Settings > Alert Preferences exposes the alert cadence as on/off toggles: payout reminder 3 days before, overdue on credit day+1, maturity alerts at 30 / 7 / 1 days, plus a daily status sweep time select (00:00-23:00). The in-app bell is always on — shown as a locked, disabled toggle with a hint. These preferences drive the credit-day engine and the alert channels from FR-33/FR-34.

sections.heading: Settings — General (D34)
sections.body: Settings > General holds app-wide defaults: default credit day for new positions (1-28 select), privacy mode on startup (toggle, default OFF), currency format (Indian ₹ 1,50,000.00 — fixed radio), table density (Compact / Comfortable radio, shared with the watchlist), and theme (Dark selected; Light disabled with 'coming later').

sections.heading: Settings — Data (D34)
sections.body: Settings > Data covers data operations: [Import from Excel...] for the legacy workbook path, [Export backup (.db)] producing a downloadable database backup, default CSV export scope select (Current view / Full ledger), and a Danger zone with [Reset local database] guarded by a typed 'RESET' confirmation.

sections.heading: Settings — About (D34)
sections.body: Settings > About shows the app version, a build-notes line, the honest '100% offline — no accounts, no cloud' badge, and an 'Open local data folder' action.

sections.heading: Shell Integration and Privacy (D33 + D34)
sections.body: The shell integrates watchlist and settings state: the status bar shows row counts matching the visible table rows and an email-status indicator ('Settings: N email alert rules active' when configured, 'Email: not configured' in muted/red otherwise). The sidebar Privacy Mode toggle masks EVERY monetary cell on the watchlist and Settings screens while names, statuses and non-money numbers stay visible (extends the D19 global Privacy Mode to the redesigned surfaces).

sections.heading: Out of Scope
sections.body: No live market data, no live rating or price feeds, no broker integrations — ratings, coupons and expected yields are manual offline entries per D33 and are labeled as manual wherever shown. No cloud, no accounts, no server: email is the only outbound network use and only when the user configures their own SMTP. Android packaging and mobile apps remain out (D27). The acceptance holds are unchanged by this addendum: import reconciliation (totals computed from the imported file — sample: 15 sample positions, e.g. Total Invested ₹5,50,000.00 — reconciled against the baseline supplied with the import (owner-specific), mismatch never force-matched) and the Phase-4 P&L acceptance.

prd_items.statement: When the watchlist redesign ships, the system SHALL present a standalone desktop-style app shell — window chrome (titlebar with menu strip and window buttons), a left sidebar navigation with the destinations Dashboard, Month Grid, Watchlist, Financial Goals, Alerts, Reports/Print and Settings (Settings being a real nav destination), and a bottom status bar — so the product reads as an app, not a website (D33).

The watchlist SHALL provide two views via segmented tabs — 'My Holdings' (owned positions) and 'Watching' (candidates being evaluated, not owned), each showing its own count; a 'Move to Holdings' action on a Watching item SHALL convert it into a held position that appears in the monthly grid and dashboard and updates the counts on both tabs, and the drawer's 'Mark as Watching' action SHALL provide the reverse move (D33).

The bond master field set SHALL be upgraded with credit rating plus rating agency, coupon %, expected yield % (manual offline entry, labeled as manual in the UI), payout cycle (Monthly/Quarterly/Annual), issuer type (Corporate Bond/NCD/SDI/Govt), secured flag, and face value — all stored per position and surfaced in the watchlist table, Watching cards and detail drawer (D33).

The watchlist table SHALL offer filter chips (rating, payout cycle, issuer type, status), text search by company or ISIN, column sorting including maturity, removable active-filter chips, and a Compact/Comfortable density switch; monetary columns SHALL be right-aligned in Indian numbering format and each row's status SHALL be indicated by a colored left border (D33).

When a watchlist row is selected, the system SHALL open a detail drawer for that position showing its facts (ISIN, face value, secured, issuer type, credit rating + agency, start date, end date, credit day with payout cycle), its payment schedule (received/overdue/upcoming with amounts), and a yield/investment summary, with the actions Edit Position, Record Payment and Mark as Watching (D33).

The watchlist SHALL include an alerts panel fed by the day-wise credit-day engine (FR-33) and the in-app notification history (FR-34), showing overdue-payout, due-soon and maturity-soon cards with dismiss buttons and alert dots on affected rows; dismissing a card SHALL remove it from the panel only and SHALL leave the notification history row with its timestamp intact (D33).

Settings SHALL include an Email Alerts screen with SMTP configuration UI — host, port with SSL (465) or STARTTLS (587) selection, username, App Password (masked on entry and never re-displayed after save), recipient and from-name — plus a Test Email button, a Save button and a configured/not-configured status badge; credentials SHALL be stored locally in alert_prefs and environment variables SMTP_USER / SMTP_APP_PASSWORD SHALL override the stored values (D34).

Settings SHALL include an Alert Preferences screen with on/off toggles for payout reminder (3 days before), overdue alert (credit day+1), maturity alerts at 30/7/1 days, a daily status sweep time select (00:00-23:00), and the in-app bell shown as a locked, always-on disabled toggle with a hint (D34).

Settings SHALL include a General screen with default credit day for new positions (1-28 select), privacy-on-startup toggle (default OFF), Indian currency format as a fixed radio (₹ 1,50,000.00), table density radio (Compact/Comfortable, shared with the watchlist), and theme selection with Dark selected and Light disabled as coming later (D34).

Settings SHALL include a Data screen with Import from Excel, Export backup (.db) producing a downloadable database file, a default CSV export scope select (Current view / Full ledger), and a Danger zone Reset local database action guarded by a typed 'RESET' confirmation (D34).
Settings SHALL include an About screen showing the app version, a build-notes line, a '100% offline — no accounts, no cloud' badge, and an 'Open local data folder' action (D34).

The shell SHALL integrate watchlist and settings state into the status bar — row counts matching the visible table rows and an email-status indicator ('Settings: N email alert rules active' when configured, 'Email: not configured' otherwise) — and the Privacy Mode toggle SHALL mask every monetary cell on the watchlist and Settings screens while names, statuses and non-money numbers stay visible (D33, D34).
